title: Adult platform reach is broad, increasingly diversified, and patterned by age and social position
source_unit: US adult survey respondent, with platform-use and frequency reports

denominator.unit: US adults in Pew/SSRS National Public Opinion Reference Survey

observations.method: Pew Research Center survey conducted by SSRS using address-based sampling and a web, mail, and phone multimode protocol; weighted to the US adult population by gender, race and ethnicity, education, and other categories.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported platform use is not logged exposure, time spent, content encountered, or account activity; platform-specific question universes and sampling error apply.
observations.subgroup: US adults; platform measures are population estimates from the 5,022-person survey.
observations.counterinterpretation: Broad reach can represent occasional or instrumental use and does not establish influence, dependence, or a common cultural experience.

denominator.unit: US adults in 2025 survey; historical comparison uses prior Pew survey waves

whatsapp_change.unit: percentage points, 23% in 2021 to about 32% in 2025

observations.method: Repeated cross-sectional comparison across Pew survey waves; the report describes YouTube and Facebook as relatively stable while TikTok, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Reddit grew.
observations.uncertainty: This is not a panel of the same adults; changes can reflect population composition, wording or mode shifts, substitution among platforms, or movement to services not measured.
observations.subgroup: US adults across the compared survey waves.
observations.counterinterpretation: Growth in platform reach does not show growth in total attention, political influence, commercial conversion, or social dependence.

denominator.unit: US adults in separate Pew American Trends Panel survey; frequency questions use platform-specific valid response bases

facebook_daily.unit: percent of US adults visiting at least once a day; 37% several times a day

youtube_daily.unit: percent of US adults visiting at least once a day; 33% several times a day

tiktok_daily_age_65_plus.unit: percent of adults ages 65 and older

observations.method: Separate Pew American Trends Panel survey of 5,123 US adults, conducted online or by live-interviewer phone and weighted to the US adult population.
observations.uncertainty: Frequency is self-reported categorical use, not minutes or passive exposure; the frequency sample and field dates differ from the 5,022-person platform-reach survey.
observations.subgroup: US adults, with age-specific estimates for daily platform use.
observations.counterinterpretation: Daily visits may be brief, purposeful, or socially useful; frequency alone does not identify compulsion, harm, or algorithmic influence.

denominator.unit: US adults in Pew/SSRS survey; subgroup estimates use question-specific valid bases

instagram_age_65_plus.unit: percent of adults ages 65 and older

observations.method: Weighted subgroup estimates reported by Pew; subgroup differences are descriptive and not causal.
observations.uncertainty: Subgroup margins of error are larger than full-sample estimates, and reported differences may reflect access, social networks, interests, platform fit, or reporting.
observations.subgroup: Age, gender, race and ethnicity, education, and partisan groups of US adults.
observations.counterinterpretation: Demographic concentration in a platform does not imply a uniform culture or political effect within that group.

related_sources.claim: Pew report, platform-use estimates, frequency estimates, historical comparisons, and methodology.

boundary: This record measures self-reported adult platform reach, frequency, change across repeated survey waves, and subgroup differences. It does not establish total attention time, content exposure, recommendation effects, political persuasion, consumer conversion, privacy loss, dependence, or causality.
